The headline is the attention step

sources.title: The psychology of curiosity: A review and reinterpretation
The Upworthy Research Archive, a time series of 32,487 experiments in U.S. media

concepts.definition: The title text a reader sees before deciding whether to open a piece of content.
Curiosity as a feeling of deprivation caused by noticing a gap between what one knows and wants to know.
A headline that promises more than the content delivers.

questions.q: Why does a curiosity headline need some prior knowledge in the reader?
questions.a: Under information gap theory, a gap is only felt against existing knowledge; people are not curious about topics they know nothing about.

questions.q: How many experiments does the Upworthy Research Archive contain, and over which period?
questions.a: 32,487 headline and image tests run between January 2013 and April 2015.

questions.q: Why should you write the headline first?
questions.a: It forces you to decide what the piece promises and keeps the writing focused; revise it at the end.
